We need a retrosynthesis route with 1 step (i.e., a single reaction) to target molecule: COC(C1(C=C1[Si](C)(C)C)/C=C/C2=CC=CC=C2)=O. This is a methyl ester of a carboxylic acid attached to a vinyl phenyl with a trimethylsilyl group on a cyclopropane? Actually structure: methyl ester of a carbonyl attached to a carbon bearing a cyclopropyl with TMS? Wait: COC( ... )=O is methyl ester of a carbonyl attached to C1(C=C1[Si](C)(C)C)/C=C/ phenyl. So the core is a 2-phenyl-2-(trimethylsilyl)cyclopropyl? Actually C1(C=C1[Si](C)(C)C) is a cyclopropane with a double bond? C1(C=C1[Si](C)(C)C) is a cyclopropene? Not sure.

Goal: find commercially available precursors that can combine in one step to give this ester. Likely a simple esterification: combine a carboxylic acid (or acid chloride) with methanol. So target is methyl ester of a carboxylic acid: O=C(OCH3)-C(...). So retrosynthesis: break ester to carboxylic acid and methanol. So precursors: the corresponding carboxylic acid: O=C(O)C(C1(C=C1[Si](C)(C)C)/C=C/C2=CC=CC=C2) and methanol (CO). Check if both are buyable and total price <=125. Need to verify buyability. Use is_buyable for acid and methanol.
